Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:169: In the Zohar (parashat Naso 145b), they explained this verse, that whoever merits fear merits humility and piety. Rabbi Elazar said, whoever possesses fear, humility, and piety possesses the totality of all. And it says there, that "those who fear Him" refers to the totality of male and female, which is "Adam" — for whoever joins male and female is called "Adam," and then he fears sins, and not only that, but humility rests upon him, and not only that, but Chesed rests upon him. And whoever does not have male and female found together has neither fear, nor humility, nor piety; therefore he is called "Adam," the totality of all, and since he is called "Adam," Chesed rests upon him, as it is written (Psalms 89:3), "I said, the world shall be built with kindness," etc. — end of quotation, as pertains here. It seems to me that his words may be understood regarding the matter of "Adam" in what is explained in the Zohar (parashat Bereishit 34b) regarding the division of the letters of "Adam"; see there, and thereby the rest of the passage is understood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:170: When a person holds fast to all these attributes of Chesed mentioned, and the other attributes stated in the passage, the holy spirit will rest upon him. It seems to me that this is what our sages, of blessed memory, meant (Bava Batra 25b): whoever wishes to become wise should turn southward — meaning, whoever wishes to merit the attribute of wisdom must hold fast to the attribute of Chesed, called "south," for Chesed is a throne to Chochmah, and by holding fast to the attributes of Chesed he will surely merit the Chochmah above it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:171: In Tanna Devei Eliyahu it says, regarding the merit of the holy spirit, in these words, in the Yalkut (Judges, siman 72, p. 9b), on the verse "and Deborah, a prophetess" (Judges 4:4): what was the nature of Deborah, that she prophesied over Israel and judged them, when Pinchas son of Elazar was still alive? I call heaven and earth to witness for me — whether gentile or Israelite, whether man or woman, whether servant or maidservant, all according to a person's deeds does the holy spirit rest upon him. The rest of his words, regarding Lapidot, need not be quoted.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:1: We thought fit in this chapter to explain that among the grades a person must reach to become a lover and a chasid, he must acquire three attributes: first, trust [bitachon]; second, faith [emunah]; third, joy [simchah]. Trust, as it is said (Psalms 32:10), "but he who trusts in the Lord, kindness shall surround him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:2: Faith — Abraham our father, peace be upon him, is the head of believers, as it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the Lord" — this is the word "emunah" first mentioned in the Torah; and so it is written in Mishneh Torah (Deuteronomy 7:9), "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and the kindness," and likewise (Deuteronomy 32:4), "a God of faithfulness and without iniquity."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:3: Further, our sages, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Shir HaShirim (4:20), and likewise in Midrash Shemot Rabbah, on the verse "then he sang," in these words: another interpretation, "look from the peak of Amanah [faith]" — this is Abraham, of whom it is written, "and he believed in the Lord." "From the peak of Senir" — this is Isaac. "And Hermon" — this is Jacob. — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:4: So too it is explained in the Tikkunim (5a) regarding "and He shall be the faithfulness of your times" (Isaiah 33:6) — that faithfulness is the order of Zera'im in Chesed, and it says: faithfulness [emunah] is the Supernal Mother, from the side of Chesed, in whom is the Shema, which is faithfulness. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:5: Joy, as explained in parashat Vayikra (Zohar 8a), that the priest is the one who brings joy, and of him it is said (Psalms 100:2), "serve the Lord with gladness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:6: Let us return to explain each and every one of these separately, and thereby the matter of complete love will be explained to you. Trust is a person's rest and repose from worry over the matter he fears, when he considers that matter as something he leans and relies upon as a shield, a buckler, and a fortified wall — and then he shall be secure and not fear that former dread, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:52), "the fortified [cities] in which you trust." The parable for this: a poor man's heart trusts in a rich man that he will support him with his generosity; likewise a mighty man trusts in his own might, and a wise man in his own wisdom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:7: Because all these things are from Him, blessed be He — I mean, from His supernal attributes toward us, He and His attributes being all one — therefore David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 31:15), "but I trust in You, O Lord," "and I have trusted in Your kindness" (ibid. 13:6), "in this I trust" (ibid. 27:3), "my heart trusted in Him, and I was helped" (ibid. 28:7), "and trust in Him, and He will act" (ibid. 37:5) — and this "in Him" [alav] is like "cast your burden upon [al] the Lord" (ibid. 55:23), which is explained in the Zohar (parashat Acharei 79b) as referring to matters that depend on mazal, which is "al" [above]. "I have trusted in the kindness of God," etc. (ibid. 52:10), "in God I have trusted, I will not fear" (ibid. 56:5), "happy is the man who trusts in You," etc. (ibid. 84:13), "his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord" (ibid. 112:7), "in the fear of the Lord is strong confidence," etc. (Proverbs 14:26), "and he who trusts in the Lord, happy is he" (ibid. 16:20), and likewise "and he who trusts in the Lord shall be made fat" (ibid. 28:25) — from these verses the place of trust will be explained to you, if you are versed in the appellations of the attributes explained in the Zohar.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:8: Rabbeinu Bachya, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, ch. 3), wrote that the premises through which a person completes his trust are these: first, that he believe that the Creator, blessed be He, has more mercy on man than any other merciful being, and that all the mercy and compassion shown him by others are all from the mercy and compassion of God, as it is said (Psalms 103:8), "the Lord is merciful and gracious," and it says (Deuteronomy 13:18), "and He will give you mercy, and have compassion on you, and multiply you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:9: The second, that the means of man's benefit are not hidden from the Creator, blessed be He, because He originated man's root, form, and constitution, and the order of his composition — He is the Wise One who knows his affairs, his benefits and his harms, and what is good for him both in his world and in his end, as it is written (Isaiah 48:17), "I am the Lord who teaches you to profit, who leads you in the way you should go."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:10: The third, that the Creator, blessed be He, is strong and cannot be overcome in what He desires, as it is written (Job 9:4), "wise of heart and mighty in strength," and His decree is issued regarding every matter, and none can turn back His judgment, as it is written, "whatever He desires, He does," etc., and it says (Isaiah 55:11), "so shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; it shall not return to Me void." Therefore there is none who can prevent Him from doing what the trusting one seeks — for if He were weak, trust in Him could not be complete.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:11: The fourth, that He knows the means of benefit for the one who trusts, and nothing is hidden from Him of what is good for him, whether hidden or manifest, and He watches over the conduct of all human beings, does not neglect them nor is unaware of them, and nothing of theirs is hidden from Him, as it is written (Psalms 121:3), "behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps," and it says (Isaiah 40:27), "why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, my way is hidden from the Lord," etc., "do you not know, have you not heard, the everlasting God," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:12: The fifth, that He is uniquely engaged in the governance of the one who trusts in Him, from the beginning of his existence — his greatness, his infancy, his youth, his old age — until the end of all his affairs, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is He not your Father who acquired you, who made you and established you," and it says (Psalms 22:10), "for You are He who drew me from the womb, who made me trust while on my mother's breasts; upon You I was cast from the womb, from my mother's belly You are my God," and it says (Job 10:10), "did You not pour me out like milk," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:13: The sixth, that the affairs of the trusting one are entrusted into His hand alone — no person can harm him or benefit him, nor push away harm from him, except by His power, blessed be He — and he is like a captive prisoner bound in a pit within his master's net. And when a person feels that no creature can benefit or harm him except with permission from the Creator, blessed be He, his heart will turn back from fearing them and will trust in the Creator, blessed be He, as it is written (Psalms 146:3), "do not trust in princes," etc., "happy is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God." And it says (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man," etc. (ibid. 17:7), "blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:14: The seventh, that he know that the One in whom he trusts is the utmost of generosity and kindness, to whoever is worthy of it and to whoever is not worthy of it, and His generosity is constant and His kindness endures, is never cut off nor ceases — and man is obligated to serve Him for the abundant kindness and good he receives from Him, without being worthy in His eyes and without any prior kindness having preceded toward Him, as He says (Job 41:3), "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?" — and as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 40:6), "many things You have done, O Lord my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us," etc., and it says (ibid. 145:9), "the Lord is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works," and it says (ibid. 136:25), "He gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever," and it says (ibid. 145:16), "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:15: Reason dictates that when these seven matters are gathered together in the Creator, blessed be He, one's trust in Him becomes strengthened and one submits to Him, does not suspect Him in His judgment, nor grow angry at His choice, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 116:3-4), "distress and sorrow I found, and I called upon the name of the Lord." — end of the summary of his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:16: When you examine these seven matters mentioned, you will find that all these actions are particular to the attribute of Chesed, blessed be He, and especially to the matter of constant providence and the kindnesses that never cease, particular to the "open eye" of Arich [Anpin], as it is written in the Idra of Naso (129-130), that this eye never sleeps nor slumbers and always watches, and it says there that it watches over all and all is sustained through it, and it further says, and this eye is the sustaining of all, and of it it is written (Proverbs 22:9), "a good eye [tov ayin] shall be blessed [yevorach]" — do not read "yevorach" but "yevarech" ["shall bless"], for this is called "good eye," and from it all is blessed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:17: The other actions mentioned, such as (Psalms 22:10), "for You are He who drew me from the womb, who made me trust while on my mother's breasts," these actions are attributed to the lower Chesed, called "Atah" ["You"] — "Atah kohen le-olam" ["You are a priest forever"], and likewise "from my mother's belly, [Atah] You are my God." And there is a providence attributed to the lower Chesed, for sight belongs to the right, as explained in the Tikkunim (122a), and they gave the sign of the face of a lion to the right, and "re'iyah" [seeing] is "aryeh" [lion]. However, this lower providence, which is in the lower eye, is at times interrupted, and therefore the Psalmist said (ibid. 44:24), "awake, why do You sleep, O Lord." However, the supernal providence never ceases.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:18: Therefore, wherever trust is found, it is the aspect of Chesed spreading throughout all the attributes, and therefore we find trust in supernal Chesed, as it is said (Psalms 21:8), "for the king trusts in the Lord, and through the kindness of the Most High he shall not be moved." And even the trust mentioned regarding Elohim, as it is said (ibid. 56:5), "in Elohim I have trusted, I will not fear," etc., the intent is regarding the aspect of Chesed within Elohim, which is El from Elohim, as it is said (ibid. 52:10), "I have trusted in the kindness of Elohim" — or the intent is regarding the totality of Chesed within the attribute of Elohim, in such a way that one who trusts in the Lord is fittingly surrounded by kindness, kindness being that which spreads throughout, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:19: Among the conditions of one who trusts is that he consider and know that the Creator sees his heart, whether his trust in Him is complete or not — for a servant serving before a king of flesh and blood can deceive his heart, but from the Creator, blessed be He, the Former of hearts, nothing is hidden, and no one can deceive Him, as it is written (Psalms 94:11), "the Lord knows the thoughts of man, that they are vanity," and it says (Proverbs 24:12), "does not He who weighs hearts perceive it, and He who guards your soul, does He not know?" and it says (II Chronicles 6:30), "for You alone know the hearts of the children of man." And he should not trust in any person without the power of the Name — as it is written (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man," etc., "and whose heart turns away from the Lord" — for all the causes that reach him, such as his food, his other acquisitions, or his healing, are all causes caused by Him, blessed be He, to bring that matter to him. Rabbeinu Bachya, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot, already likened this in his book (Gate of Trust, ch. 3) to a water-wheel that draws water from a well through prepared vessels — for if one of them is lacking, the drawing of water is prevented.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:20: I further found written a fitting parable on this matter: like blind men walking one after another, each one placing his hand on his fellow's shoulder, but all being drawn along by the first one, who can see — and if this one should slip away from them, they would all stumble and fall. So it is fitting for a person to think that there is no guide except Him, blessed be He, the one who is exalted above all, and from Him all causes and intermediaries are set in motion to bring the desired thing to him — a remedy through a certain drug, through a certain treatment, and similarly with other worldly matters, such as a craft that is a cause for his livelihood — he should not trust in that cause, for if that cause were nullified, his livelihood and sustenance would not therefore be lacking, for the Holy One, blessed be He, would provide for him through another means — like a person chopping wood with an axe: although the axe cuts the wood, the power does not come from the axe but from the man chopping — as it is written (Isaiah 10:15), "shall the axe boast itself over him who chops with it?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:21: Among the matters of trust, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (ibid.) that one's diligence and effort should be great to fulfill what the Creator has obligated him regarding His service, and to perform His commandments, and to be careful about what He has warned against, so that the Creator will concur with him in what he trusts Him for — as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot 2:4), "do His will as your own will, so that He do your will as His will; nullify your will before His will," etc. And Scripture says (Psalms 37:3), "trust in the Lord and do good, dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness," and it says (Lamentations 3:25), "the Lord is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that seeks Him." But whoever trusts in the Creator while rebelling against Him — how foolish he is, and how weak his understanding and perception! For you see that whoever among people is appointed by someone over a matter, when he commands him to engage in what is needed, or warns him against certain things, and he transgresses his command, thereby reaching his appointer's transgression against his command, this becomes a strong cause preventing what he trusted from being done for him — how much more so one who transgresses the statutes and commandments of God, which He has designated and testified about, that the hope of the one trusting in Him be disappointed when he rebels against Him, and it is not fitting that he be called "one who trusts in God," but rather he is as Scripture says (Job 27:8), "for what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he has gained, when God takes away his soul? Will God hear his cry?" etc., and it says (Jeremiah 7:9-10), "will you steal, murder," etc., "and come and stand before Me in this house"? — end of quotation. And I say that of this it is said (Proverbs 14:16), "but the fool rages and is confident."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:22: Likewise it is fitting that he not trust in his wealth, as it is said (ibid. 11:28), "he who trusts in his riches shall fall" — for everything is from Him, as it is said (I Chronicles 29:14), "for everything is from You, and from Your own hand we have given You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:23: Likewise, among the matters of trust, that he not trust in his good deeds, that through them he will be saved from the mishaps of the world and from severe illnesses — for if so, he consumes his merits — but rather he should trust in His kindness, for his deeds do not suffice to repay the debts he owes the Creator, as the pious author elaborated at length in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, ch. 4) — that even if his deeds were doubled and redoubled, they would not suffice to repay even one of the Creator's kindnesses toward him. Rather, he should think that just as He, blessed be He, gives sustenance to all creatures, to roots, to animals, beasts, and birds, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 107b), He sits and sustains from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice — just as He has mercy on these not for their deeds but through His great mercies, so shall He have mercy on him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:24: The particulars of trust are many, and this is but a very small amount gleaned from what the pious author explained in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust). In general, one who trusts is fittingly called a chasid, and is a chariot for the attribute of Chesed, like Abraham — for just as the chasid is called a lover, and the lover's way is to cling to the love of the Creator, as it is said (Proverbs 18:24), "there is a lover who clings closer than a brother," as we elaborated at length in the preceding chapters, and loves nothing besides the Creator — so one who trusts does not trust in creatures, nor does he place the strength of his condition upon them, but rather upon the Creator. It follows that since his trust in Him is a clinging to Him, he loves Him — and this is what the author of Chovot HaLevavot, peace be upon him, explained, that one who trusts is fittingly submitted to His judgment like Abraham our father when he was thrown into the fiery furnace, and likewise the matter of Chananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, etc., which we quoted above (ch. 6).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:25: So too you find regarding Abraham our father, peace be upon him, that he was tested with ten trials, and had it not been for his trust in the Creator, blessed be He, and his firmness in the cords of His love, he would have rebelled; and it is written (Nehemiah 9:8), "and You found his heart faithful [ne'eman] before You" — "ne'eman" means strong and enduring, unwavering — and this is the meaning of "ne'eman" found throughout the Torah, such as (I Kings 11:38), "and I will build for you a faithful house," and the opposite of this (Genesis 45:26), "and his heart fainted, for he did not believe them." And likewise regarding the fulfillment and firmness of a statement, it is said (Numbers 5:22), "and the woman shall say, amen, amen." There is no need to elaborate on this further, as it is simple.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:26: It follows that one who believes and one who trusts are both one matter, for one who trusts also has his heart supported and firm regarding the desired thing, in the One who will fulfill it for him, as explained above. And I found it written that it is impossible to be trusting without being believing, and faith in God, blessed be He, is what brings a person to trust — for since he believes in the Creator, blessed be He, he understands that his success, both in this world and in the World to Come, all comes from Him, and there is none other besides Him; then he sets his heart to trust in Him and to love Him with all his heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:27: What brings a person to be a believer is that he not fear any evil thing, but rather accept everything that comes upon him with joy — and he resembles a servant who recognizes that his master is generous and has a good eye, and at the time he burdens his servants with hard labor, he then bestows upon them great favors and elevates and exalts them, and they become his counselors and eat from his table and are set upon his second chariot and appointed over his treasury. There is no doubt that this servant, knowing and recognizing this about his master, would abandon everything in the world in order to do his master's will with joy — and although that labor would be very hard for him to perform, when he remembers the good that will reach him on account of that labor, everything becomes easy for him. But a servant who sees his master as stingy and his labor greater than his wage does not labor except in sorrow. So too the matter: whoever truly believes that everything he does and labors for in the Creator's service is all for his own good, and that the Holy One, blessed be He, will give him a good and great reward for all he endures for His great Name, and for all the service and ministry he performs for the sake of Heaven He will give him pleasantness in the World to Come — in the manner we find regarding Nebuchadnezzar, that for the four steps he took in honor of the Creator he merited great greatness in this world (Sanhedrin 96a), and also Esau, for honoring his father and mother, merited greatness in this world, he and his descendants after him, and likewise many similar cases — there is no doubt that when a person believes all this with a whole heart, he will surely rejoice in all of God's decrees, for who would not rejoice at giving a penny to charity for the sake of Heaven, and being given in its stead in the World to Come a talent of gold?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:28: Whoever believes in God with a whole heart will believe in the punishment of the sinner, and will not come to sin; and therefore the entire Torah depends on faith — for how is the beginning of the Torah? "I am the Lord your God... you shall have no other gods before Me" (Exodus 20:2-3) — and if one does not believe, what use is his Torah? At a time when a person believes from the depth of his heart that the Creator will fulfill everything written in His Torah, to punish the sinner — and He is witness — and brings good reward to whoever fulfills His Torah, then he keeps the Torah — for surely, if the thief and the robber knew that they would be killed and could not escape, they would restrain themselves from theft and robbery; but they think and trust that they will be saved — therefore the whole Torah is entirely included within faith, as it is written (Habakkuk 2:4), "and the righteous shall live by his faith," and regarding Abraham it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the Lord, and He counted it to him as righteousness" — and regarding all the other things he did, righteousness is not written except regarding faith. And of this it is said (Numbers 12:7), "in all My house he is faithful."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:29: I further say that all the commandments that depend on tradition require faith, and if one does not believe, he demolishes the entire Torah — for if one does not believe that this is the Torah of Moses given to us, and likewise the tradition of the scribes, who explained thus regarding the commandments of sukkah and lulav and the like, then he denies the Torah. Similarly, the matters we have by tradition, which our sages, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Berachot (54a) — one who sees the stone Moses sat upon, and the fords of the Jordan, or the place of the altar Elijah made on Carmel — for all these things depend on tradition, and likewise that this is the Temple and this is Jerusalem and the like — all these require faith; and if he believes in these, his soul will be enflamed with love of the Creator when he remembers the miracles He performed for us in those places; but if he does not believe, surely he has no love for the Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:30: They said in the Midrash, brought in the Yalkut (parashat Beshalach, siman 240, p. 69c), on the verse "and they believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant": as reward for the faith they believed, the holy spirit rested upon them and they sang a song, as it is written (Exodus 15:1), "then Moses and the children of Israel sang." Rabbi Nechemyah says: from where do you say that whoever accepts upon himself even one commandment with faith is worthy of having the holy spirit rest upon him? For so we find that our forefathers, as reward for the faith they believed, etc. — you find that our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt only by the merit of faith, as it is said (Exodus 4:31), "and the people believed," and so it says (Psalms 31:24), "the Lord preserves the faithful."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:31: Further it says: "this is the gate of the Lord, the righteous shall enter through it" (ibid. 118:20) — regarding the possessors of faith, what does it say? (Isaiah 26:2), "open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter" — through this gate all possessors of faith enter. And so it says (Psalms 92:2), "it is good to give thanks to the Lord" — what brought them to this joy? Only the merit of faith, that their forefathers believed in this world, which is entirely nights; therefore it says (ibid. 92:3), "to declare Your kindness in the morning," etc. And so Jehoshaphat said to the people (II Chronicles 20:20), "believe in the Lord your God, and you shall be established; believe His prophets, and you shall succeed." "O Lord, do Your eyes not look for faithfulness?" (Jeremiah 5:3). "But the righteous shall live by his faith" (Habakkuk 2:4). "They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:23). Likewise you find that the exiles are gathered in only by the merit of faith, as it is said (Song of Songs 4:8), "come with me from Lebanon, bride," etc., "look from the peak of Amanah"; "and I will betroth you to Me forever, and I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness" (Hosea 2:21-22). Behold, how great is faith before Him who spoke and the world came to be — for as reward for the faith they believed, the holy spirit rested upon them and they sang a song, as it is said (Exodus 14:31), "and they believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant," "then Moses sang." And so it says (Psalms 106:12), "then they believed His words, they sang His praise." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:32: The reason faith is associated with Chesed is already quoted at the beginning of the chapter, the language of the Tikkunim (5a), which said that in it is the Shema, which is faith. The meaning is that of the four passages in the tefillin, the third passage is Chesed, and in the third passage we mention the faith of unity, "the Lord our God, the Lord is One"; and so the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (parashat Bo 43b), which we quoted above in chapter 5, saying: the third passage, Shema, this is the secret of the right, called "supernal Chesed," which unifies the unity of all in four directions, and the Holy One, blessed be He, arranges through it the order of the whole world, and this is what spreads even into the lowest depths. — end of quotation. Through the Chesed that spreads into all creatures, as it says that it spreads even into the depths, the creatures believe in Him and in His unity — therefore the word "emunah" [faith] first mentioned in the Torah is mentioned regarding Abraham, as it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the Lord" — for through Abraham the true faith was revealed in the world, as explained in the Zohar, that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, would inform all who came into the world that there is a Creator who created everything and whose kindness is available to all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:33: With this one may understand what is said in the Zohar (end of parashat Vayelech), that whoever answers "amen" over each and every blessing — just as he thereby opens the supernal gates, the gates of the supernal flow, so shall they open for his soul when it departs this world, as it is said (Isaiah 26:2), "open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith [shomer emunim] may enter" — do not read "emunim" but "amenim." The reason is that the opening of gates is from the side of Chesed, as explained in the Tikkunim (38b), "open for me" on the first day; and likewise the opening [petach] with vowel-points is Chochmah, as explained in the Tikkunim (128) — and reason dictates that the King opens gates only from the side of His great kindness and simple will, for from the side of judgment He would close the flow, but through Chesed it is opened — this being "You open Your hand" — and since one who answers "amen" opens the gates through Chesed, so it is fitting that they open for him in the future.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:34: It follows that through His bestowal of kindness upon us, we drive our faith into Him; this is what Scripture says (Lamentations 3:23), "new every morning; great is Your faithfulness" — for through the kindness He performs with us every morning, in that we deposit with Him our weary soul, and He returns it to us renewed, and all that weariness it had is gone, and it is a new soul as at the beginning of its creation — this is a great kindness, and this renewal is surely from the side of Chesed, for the meaning is "who renews in His goodness, every day continually, the work of creation" (blessing of Yotzer Or) — particularly in the mornings, which is "the morning of Abraham" (Zohar, parashat Mishpatim 119b). Through this, "great is Your faithfulness" — that we have great faith afterward to deposit our souls each night in His hand, remembering the kindness He performs with us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:35: Let us return to the exposition we were engaged in — that trust and faith are partners with one another, for whoever believes in God with a whole heart trusts in Him with a strong trust, and trust will bring him not to fear anything, and not to serve any person besides the Creator, for He is God, and not to hope in any man, nor agree with them in a matter contrary to the service of God, nor to fear their affairs, nor be afraid of their disputes — and if he rebukes them, he will not be careful about their honor nor be ashamed before them nor beautify falsehood for them, as the prophet said (Isaiah 50:7), "and the Lord God will help me, therefore I have not been humiliated" — and his trust will bring him to turn away from worldly affairs and dedicate his heart to matters of Torah and service. This is impossible unless his trust is great in YHVH, and therefore his reward is great, that he becomes bound to Chesed, as it is written (Psalms 32:10), "and he who trusts in the Lord, kindness shall surround him." And it says "shall surround him," meaning that Chesed shall encircle him and clothe him, in the manner of (Exodus 21:8), "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her," which is explained in the Sabba [Zohar] (96b) as referring to garments of honor from the side of the name "Eloha," which is Chesed. And the reason he said "in YHVH" is that YHVH is the root of all the Names and of all beings, and since he places his trust in the very essence of everything, that which sustains everything and brings into existence him, his spirit, and his soul — he is removed from all the mishaps of the world, and Chesed conceals him from all the possessors of judgment, as it is said (Psalms 91:2-4), "I say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress, for He shall deliver you from the snare of the fowler," etc., "with His wings He shall cover you, and under His wings you shall take refuge," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:36: Among the conditions of the faithful and trusting one is to be faithful in his service to the Creator, like a peg fixed in a faithful place that shall not be moved — for the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "the faithful God who keeps the covenant and the kindness," etc. (Deuteronomy 7:9), and His kindness is always extended to all creatures, and it is inconceivable that His kindness be removed from creatures, Heaven forbid, and be nullified for even a moment; rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant and a decree in His kindness with creatures, that His kindness never depart from them — and this is why we find in the Torah "covenant" adjacent to "kindness," as in (Deuteronomy 7:12), "the Lord your God will keep for you the covenant and the kindness," and so the prophet said (Isaiah 54:10), "for the mountains shall depart," etc., "but My kindness shall not depart from you, and My covenant of peace shall not be moved," etc. It follows that whoever is faithful in His words, His commandments, and His Torah, is bound to Chesed and Tzedek [righteousness] as one.
